newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, may fall further.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, may fall further.

text.p: Gold prices may be heading lower on Wednesday after a rally late on Tuesday attracted sufficient selling to turn the market, dealers said.
The positive response of the financial markets to U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins Testimony to Congress on Tuesday halted gold's nascent rally.
Greenspan said U.S. economic growth was slowing and that inflation in 1997 was modest, avoiding the need for near-term monetary policy tightening.
He said little price pressure was evident in the agricultural or industrial commodity sectors.
"We are now beginning also to see a very marked decline in long term inflation expectations," he added.
Gold was fixed at $324.35 per ounce, down from $328.25 on Tuesday afternoon and a close of $327.80/$328.30.

The market had been steady to firm most of Tuesday and edged higher on news that South Africa's Western Areas mine had bought 1.6 million ounces of gold from the market as it restructured a 7.3 million ounce hedge established in 1995.
The purchase was to allow the company to benefit more from any rise in the gold price, the company said.
"The Western Areas purchase has all been done otherwise they wouldn't have announced it and there was good selling into the rally the news brought," a dealer said.
Later details of Greenspan's congressional testimony sent the stock and bond markets racing higher.
The prospect of mild inflation, no immediate need to raise interest rates and the Dow closing up over 150 points did little to enhance gold's attraction as an investment, dealers said.
"I can see gold going back to its breakout point (for the last rally) at $321-$322. If it falls through $320.00 that would not be good," a dealer said.
Silver was off with gold at $3.29/$3.31, down seven cents.

Platinum and palladium attracted interest as continuing concerns about the reliability of Russia's delayed 1997 deliveries to Japan and Europe were encouraging covering in an already tight market, dealers said.
However, some dealers argued that the rally which had taken platinum to around $422.00 on Tuesday was played out and lower prices were ahead.
Platinum was at $416.0/$419.00, down $1.50, and palladium was up about $3.50 at $201.00/$204.00
